statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases again because the overnight Iran-strike range has now held for a third consecutive hour with price mid-range, while Stress stays elevated on an oil, geopolitical, rate-path and month-end catalyst stack.
recommendation: Conditions are described as two-way inside an unchanged roughly 271-point overnight range against an elevated event backdrop. A narrow evidence-based danger window is flagged from 13:30 to 16:00 UTC around the U.S. cash open and the 14:30 UTC Dallas Fed release, where the mapped state moves to WATCH.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a third hour inside a 271-point overnight range near 29,460 as Brent steadies at $91 after renewed US-Iran strikes
body: U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, breaking up an attempted mining operation, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they fired missiles at U.S. bases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, with Jordanian forces intercepting eight of them. Kharg Island, which handles roughly 90% of Iran's crude exports, has been publicly threatened, and the U.S. Treasury has flagged secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners. Brent trades near $91.06, up about 3.4%, with WTI near $86.13, up about 3.3%; both are flat to marginally lower than an hour ago rather than extending. Nasdaq-100 futures fell to 29,274.75 on the overnight headlines, fully retraced, extended to 29,545.50, and trade near 29,458.50, down about 0.11%. That 29,274.75-29,545.50 range is now unchanged across three consecutive hourly assessments, neither extreme has been retested, and price sits mid-range. S&P 500 futures near 7,706.75 are down 0.20% inside an unchanged 7,684.25-7,724.00 range, having ticked lower without widening that range. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Friday at 29,433.43 after a 0.70% decline. The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.737% and the 30-year 5.227% as of 10:29 UTC, each up only one to two basis points. VIX is 15.28 with a 14.89-15.31 day range, up about 5.9% from Friday's 14.43 close but still low in absolute terms. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks lifted September rate-hike odds to roughly 57-62% from about 41% a week earlier. European equities opened little changed, with the Stoxx 600 marginally lower and energy leading. The decisive observation for this assessment is that a third full hour has passed with both range extremes rejected and neither retested, while oil has stopped extending; that is direct evidence mean reversion is functioning. The amplifier count remains high but observed price-path structure stays two-sided. Today is the last trading session of August, so month-end rebalancing is an additional mechanical factor into the 20:00 UTC close. The Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index at 14:30 UTC has not yet been released and is carried as a scheduled checkpoint. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was about 287 minutes old at assessment time and was therefore treated as stale under the inherited freshness rule and used for discovery only, with all levels above taken from independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments were available and every one mapped to EA_ON. Tail held at 5 through the Sunday reopen window, rose to 15 at 00:00 UTC as the Iran escalation was first priced, decayed back to 5 by 07:00-08:00 UTC, jumped to a peak of 17 at 09:00 UTC as oil extended, then eased to 11 and 10 over the following two hours. Stress climbed from 26 to a peak of 52 and has since drifted to 49. Dominant mode moved from normal to mixed after 23:00 UTC, with one trend-down hour at 00:00 UTC and event/whipsaw at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC. The pattern is an event shock that was absorbed rather than extended.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps the mapped state at EA_ON for 22 of 24 hours. Conditional Tail runs 9 now and 16 into the cash-open approach, reaching 21 and 20 for the two hours inside the flagged 13:30-16:00 UTC danger window, where the mapped state becomes WATCH. It steps down to 13-15 through the U.S. afternoon, rises to 17 into the 20:00 UTC month-end close, then settles to a 9-11 overnight baseline across the Asian session before drifting to 10-13 as the September 1 ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS block at 14:00 UTC approaches from just outside the horizon. Stress peaks near 57 around the cash open and decays toward 40-45 overnight. Confidence declines from 86 to 60 with horizon.
